label: Federated tenant posture
query: What should Lakeshore L0 see that Morgan Street L1 should not automatically see at transaction grain?
answer: My read For Lakeshore Holdings, L0 should see tenant-spanning patterns and metadata about transactions, but not raw transaction-level content from any single tenant that Morgan Street L1 could drill into. L0 is about posture and governance; L1 is about doing work on specific tenant data. Why 1) You already have a federated substrate: 1,329 inventory records across 9 segments in Azure AI Search with tenant-scoped grounding. That’s the right line: L0 should lean on summary views over that substrate, not break tenant scopes. 2) Your current proof question is “Federated tenant posture” — posture means cross-tenant health and coverage, not cross-tenant content. 3) Azure private plane is only “pilot-substrate healthy,” so you should err conservative on who sees transaction grain until private-plane cutover and approval-ledger are complete. Concretely, at transaction grain: L0 can see (cross-tenant, including Morgan Street) Counts, coverage, and quality metrics: number of transactions, missing fields, schema drift, ingestion freshness, error rates, lineage flags. Risk and classification metadata: PII/PHI flags, regulatory domain tags, country/region, criticality ratings, model-risk or fair-lending tags. Aggregated patterns: top 10 data sources by transaction volume, % of transactions with full lineage, distribution of transaction types by banner/portfolio entity. L0 must not automatically see (for any tenant, including Morgan Street) Raw payloads: full transaction records, unmasked IDs, customer/vendor/account identifiers, narrative fields, or documents attached to individual transactions.
